thread:
clara: Heads-up: our pre-release SAST/DAST pipeline started returning hundreds of spurious findings after a PR that removed a KMS grant. The scanner logs show KMS decrypt failures, then the triage queue blew up because missing fixtures look like code issues. Anyone here touch key bindings? :frowning:

diego: That was my change (PR 6019). I tightened keystore permissions to follow least-priv but didn't map all pipelines that fetch encrypted test data. I can revert, but we should avoid flip-flopping without a plan.

meera: sample log from the SAST runner: 
"ERROR: unable to open test-fixture.json: KMS decrypt failed: PermissionDenied
Caused by: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt denied for serviceAccount:ci-fixtures@redwood-prod"

sec-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-KMS-PROV-334999. Owner: diego. Evidence retention: 21d (SOC2 evidence window).

clara: important: these runs are part of our compliance evidence bundle. We can't just drop artifacts. We need to preserve original scanner outputs and annotate them as infra-fail so auditors can see root cause. Can SecOps apply a retention + annotation?

audit-bot: Evidence freeze applied to affected runs. Tag: compliance:SEC-2026-KMS-PROV. Retention set to 21d.

diego: I'll revert the IAM change now and then open a scoped follow-up. Quick revert terraform snippet: 
resource "google_project_iam_member" "ci_keystore_decrypt" {
  project = "redwood-prod"
  role    = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  member  = "serviceAccount:ci-fixtures@redwood-prod"
}
I'll include a TTL annotation and link to this incident.

infra-sre: Before revert, can someone run an audit query so we capture DENIED vs missing logs? Use: 
'gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"serviceAccount:ci-fixtures@redwood-prod\" AND protoPayload.methodName:kms.cryptoKeyVersions.*Decrypt" --limit=50 --format=json'
This will be attached to the ticket.

meera: ran it: we have DENIED entries at 05:12:23 and 05:12:59. No anomalies in logging ingestion for that minute. Looks like RBAC is root cause.

infra-sre: applying revert in infra-prod (terraform apply). ETA ~2m.

oncall-sre: revert applied. Confirmed audit logs show SUCCESS after revert. New SAST run pulled fixtures OK.

clara: thanks. two compliance follow-ups: 1) add a mandatory checklist item to SDLC PRs that touch cloudkms or keystore resources: include (a) smoke decrypt run output, (b) audit log query for the SA, (c) an impact statement referencing any compliance bundles. 2) require PRs to use key-level IAM when possible and to document TTL for temporary grants.

meera: technical follow-ups I'd add: - prefer SA impersonation (short-lived tokens) for CI jobs: e.g., use workload identity pools or impersonate-service-account in runners so we avoid permanent project-level bindings; - add an infra-smoke job 'infra-smoke/kms-prove' that triggers when terraform diff contains 'google_kms' and runs a decrypt + log-check; - alert on >2 PERMISSION_DENIED kms.Decrypt for any keystore SA in 5m and page infra-sre.

diego: agree. I'll update PR 6019 to reapply with a key-scoped google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member binding, plus a 1h TTL expressed in PR body and a template impact statement. I'll also add instructions to use impersonation pattern.

clara: SecOps: please apply a label 'compliance:infra-fail:SEC-2026-KMS-PROV' to the affected SAST runs and mark any findings as 'infra:degraded' so triage avoids false positives but auditors can still see them.

sec-bot: Label compliance:infra-fail:SEC-2026-KMS-PROV applied. Findings annotated as infra:degraded. Evidence retained 21d.

infra-sre: I'll create INFRA-332 to add: 1) infra-smoke/kms-prove preflight job (decrypt + log check), 2) terraform pre-merge hook that looks for cloudkms resources, 3) metric alert on KMS decrypt denials. Assigning to infra team.

meera: one extra: update our SAST/DAST triage runbook to include a step for quickly checking 'is this an infra-decrypt failure?' and a mapping to the compliance label so triage can triage less noise during compliance windows.

clara: awesome. owners: diego (PR update + scoped grant + TTL), infra-sre (INFRA-332), meera (triage runbook update), sec-ops (apply labels + evidence retention). I'll close the incident once PR lands and infra ticket is created. thanks all. :thumbsup:
